Spatial Viz
- 3 types of spatial viz: Point Maps, Contour Maps, Choropleth Maps
- Point Maps are for plotting locations of individual observations
- Contour Maps are for plotting the density or distribution of observations
- Choropleth Maps plotting outcomes in different regions
- Requires two pieces, polygons →boundaries of area (countries, states, etc) and values to color polygons or coordinates of points of interest to show on map

Effective Viz
- Ineffective visualizations are broken down into 3 categories: wrong, bad, and ugly
- Is the graph right → right for data, appropriate for story, clear purpose, not misleading, etc.
- Is the graph complete → title, subtitle, axes labelled, legend title, legend labels, caption, etc.
-Is the graph accessible → color (fill, border, bg, text), alt-text, text size
Everything added to the graph needs to be intentional

Wrangling
- All 6 verbs are stored in the dplyr package
- The 6 verbs are *select* (selects a subset of columns), *filter* (filter out or obtain a subset of the rows), *mutate* (mutate or create a column), *group_by* (group the rows by a specified column), *summarize* (calculate a numerical summary of a column), and *arrange* (arrange the rows according to some column)
